title: Bearing Life in Years by Operating Schedule
description: Type the L-10 bearing life in years for three rating-and-schedule challenges before a bar chart reveals it, then choose any of the five L-10 ratings and compare L-10 and L-50 years across five operating schedules.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Converting L-10 and L-50 bearing life from hours to years
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the L-10 and L-50 bearing life in years from a rated L-10 life in hours and an operating schedule, to within 0.1 year.

accessibility.notes: Chart canvas has an aria-label; verdicts and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; progress chips use glyphs; L-10 bars are solid and L-50 bars are light with a heavy outline, and every bar carries its value as text; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge; the rating menu works with the arrow keys.

equations: Hours per year = hours per day x days per week x 52
L-10 years = L-10 hours / hours per year
L-50 hours = 5 x L-10 hours; L-50 years = L-50 hours / hours per year
rules: Answers are judged within ±0.1 year of the unrounded model value.
Ratings and schedules are limited to the five listed values each.
assumptions: 52 operating weeks per year, as in Chapter 3 and FanPedia page 90.
limitations: L-10 and L-50 are statistical lives of a bearing population, not the life of any one bearing.

sources: FanPedia, page 90 (L-10 and L-50 definitions, L-50 = 5 x L-10, TCF ratings, example values for 40,000 h and 20,000 h)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict then reveal: commit a number, then read it on the chart
keyQuestions: Why does the same bearing last 4.6 years for one customer and 9.6 for another?
How many times longer is L-50 than L-10?
commonMisconceptions: L-10 life is the life of every bearing (it is when 10 percent are expected to have failed).
L-50 life is twice L-10 (it is five times L-10).
A bearing rated in hours lasts the same number of years for every customer (years depend on the schedule).
assessmentOpportunities: 'Challenges correct: n of 3' running score; mastery is 3 of 3 on the first attempt.
